ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: to raise up and make prominent.
EvidenceBody: Chan records make it a public teaching-seat verb: the identified master proclaims the sect's purport, presents 'this matter' before the assembly, or is asked in an interview to present a cited event. One opening discourse pairs opening the hall with 'proclaiming the teaching of the school'; another records a whisk transmitted with the charge to present this matter before the human and heavenly assembly. A later discourse says that one sentence had already been presented before the listeners entered the gate.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The stored cases establish the corpus-specific deployment of 舉揚 stated in the opening.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: No definition formula was found. The deviation is institutional and observable: the ordinary verb becomes a recurrent description of the identified master's public work from the teaching seat. The corpus does not support separate senses for different subjects raised; all are objects of the same transitive act.
DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases retrieve the same attested referent as to raise and proclaim.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The complete cases were retested for incompatible referents; this sense denotes to raise and proclaim, not a grammatical paraphrase.
